current_source_line: All nine candidates share the core-area budget and DP-array power limit of $1:2:4$ ($\beta=1$). The baseline has 36 cores, each with 256 DPs at 1\,GHz and one request per cycle. We set the baseline array-area fraction to $\alpha=0.327$, referencing the reported 32.7\% Cube-cluster share of AI Core area~\cite{luo2024hifloat8area}, and fix peripheral storage and control area per core. Single-DP area and the maximum measured power across precision modes determine the integer core counts allowed by each budget; the smaller count determines deployment. Multiplying this count by DPs per core and precision-specific DP throughput gives chip-level peak throughput. Deployment remains fixed across workloads.

current_source_line: AI workloads mix precisions and shift toward lower precision, so splitting tensor-core peak throughput across 16/8/4-bit floating-point formats becomes a key design choice. DP-Puzzle combines shared multi-precision datapaths with precision-specific compute units to tune throughput allocation; we compare nine configurations, jointly modeling area, power, and precision migration. At 12 nm and 1 GHz, doubling FP4 throughput raises area by 33.6\% while improving area and energy efficiency by 49.7\% and 27.3\%. At matched area and power, 1:2:8 performs best overall among the nine, yielding a modeled 1.13× compute-only speedup on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GEMMs. Moderate expansion thus balances low-precision capacity and deployment density.

current_source_line: Two Lanes form a T2H4Q8E16 Group, matching NVFP4's 16-element scaling block; larger blocks broadcast the same scale factor across Groups. The Group first combines the Lane results and separates the sign and magnitude, then applies the shared scale factors. Only NVFP4/HiF4 require scale-significand multiplication. The two four-bit scale significands are premultiplied into an eight-bit coefficient. After removing structurally zero low-order bits, the 14-bit Group magnitude is multiplied by this coefficient using a shared $14\times8$ multiplier. The resulting 22-bit value is mapped to the U31 magnitude interface. MX's E8M0 scale factors contribute only to the exponent.

After removing structurally zero low-order bits, the 14-bit Group magnitude is multiplied by this coefficient using a shared $14\times8$ multiplier. The resulting 22-bit value is mapped to the U31 (31-bit unsigned magnitude) interface. MX's E8M0 scale factors contribute only to the exponent.
